headline: Revenue and profit surge, aided by a disposition gain
summary_short: Corpay's Q1 2026 revenue rose 25% y/y to $1,261.0M (11% organic) and GAAP diluted EPS grew 49% to $5.07, boosted by an ~$81M/$1.19-per-share gain on the sale of its PaybyPhone business; adjusted diluted EPS was $5.80, up 29%.
summary_long: Revenue rose 25.4% y/y to $1,261.0M, with 11% organic growth led by Corporate Payments (+16% organic) and a sequential improvement in Lodging. Operating income grew 48.9% to $636.2M and net income rose 44.1% to $350.1M, lifted by a $121.4M gain on the PaybyPhone disposition (adding ~$81M to net income, ~$1.19 to diluted EPS). Adjusted EBITDA rose 24% to $688.6M on high revenue flow-through. The company repurchased 2.4 million shares for $786M and ended the quarter with $2.5B cash and 2.7x leverage. Corpay raised FY2026 guidance: revenue to $5.250-5.330B, adjusted diluted EPS to $26.30-27.10. Q2 2026 revenue is guided to ~$1.295B and adjusted diluted EPS to $6.45-6.65.

drivers.explanation: 11% organic growth led by Corporate Payments (+16% organic) on new payables and cross-border enterprise clients, plus a sequential improvement in Lodging; FX and the Alpha acquisition added to reported growth.
Includes a $121.4M gain on disposition of the PaybyPhone business within Vehicle Payments, which drove Vehicle Payments segment operating income up 72% y/y.
Operating income growth plus the PaybyPhone disposition gain, added about $81M to net income and $1.19 to diluted EPS per the company's own disclosure.
Net income growth combined with a lower diluted share count (68.4M vs 71.6M a year ago) after repurchasing 2.4 million shares for $786M in the quarter.
Revenue over-performance had high flow-through, lifting EBITDA margins over 100 basis points above the company's own expectations for the quarter.
Management raised full-year 2026 guidance, citing first-quarter over-performance, fundamental trends running ahead of expectations, and higher expected fuel prices for the rest of the year.
